# dotagent — LLM context (single-fetch digest)

> Polyglot agent orchestrator. You write `agent.toml` + a script in any
> language. dotagent schedules, supervises, retries, and notifies on
> failure from a single daemon that launchd / systemd keeps alive.
>
> This file is a dense, single-page reference optimized for LLMs. After
> reading this you should be able to write a working agent without
> opening any other doc. Links to deep dives are at the bottom.
>
> Source repo: https://github.com/avelino/dotagent
> Site (humans): https://avelino.gitbook.io/dotagent (or the `docs/`
> tree of the repo)
> Spec version: tracks `crates/dotagent-core` — when in doubt, the
> Rust source under `dotagent-core/src/manifest.rs` wins.

---

## 1. Mental model in 60 seconds

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    os["launchd / systemd<br/>(keeps the daemon alive)"] --> daemon["dotagent daemon<br/>(single process)"]
    daemon --> script["your script<br/>(any language)"]
```

- The OS scheduler (launchd on macOS / systemd on Linux) keeps the
  **daemon** alive — one unit, `run.avelino.dotagent`. It does not know
  about individual agents or schedules.
- One daemon, N agents, M schedules per agent.
- The daemon computes the single next event across every schedule and
  sleeps until then, waking early for signals. There is no per-agent
  plist and no per-agent systemd timer.
- Inbound triggers do **not** go through that loop: a worker task drains
  them beside it, so a slow scheduled run no longer holds queued chat
  messages.
- Telegram and the local Unix-socket API enter a trigger gateway that applies
  admission, per-conversation FIFO ordering, delivery shaping, and a default
  cap of four concurrent conversations.
- Your agent script just reads env vars and exits with a code.
- Failure path: retry → exhaust retries → fire `[[notifiers]]` (built-in,
  in-process) and/or `[[on_failure]]` plugins (subprocess, JSON stdio).

---

## 2. TL;DR — 3 files = 1 working agent

```
~/.config/dotagent/agents/my-agent/
├── agent.toml      # manifest (contract)
└── agent.fish      # script (or agent.py / agent.go / a binary)
```

Smallest viable manifest:

```toml
[agent]
name = "my-agent"
timeout_seconds = 300

[run]
command = "python3"
args = ["./agent.py"]

[[schedules]]
id = "every-90"
type = "interval"
interval_minutes = 90

[[notifiers]]
driver = "desktop"
events = ["given_up"]
```

The script:

```python
import os
print(f"hello from {os.environ['AGENT_NAME']}")
# exit 0 = success; any non-zero = attempt_failed
```

Install:

```bash
dotagent doctor                # validate
dotagent run my-agent          # foreground smoke test
dotagent install               # write launchd plist / systemd unit
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" ~/Library/LaunchAgents/run.avelino.dotagent.plist
```

---

## 3. `agent.toml` — every field

```toml
# ─── [agent] — identity (required) ────────────────────────────────────
[agent]
name = "my-agent"                  # REQUIRED. Unique within dotagent root.
description = "What it does."      # optional
monitor = true                     # default true. false = excluded from `tick`
timeout_seconds = 1800             # default 1800. Hard kill (SIGTERM→SIGKILL).

# ─── [run] — how to invoke (required) ─────────────────────────────────
[run]
command = "fish"                   # REQUIRED. Executable.
args = ["./agent.fish"]            # static argv prefix
working_dir = "."                  # optional, relative to manifest dir
protocol = "assistant-v1"           # optional one-shot assistant stdout protocol

# ─── [env] — environment injection (optional) ─────────────────────────
[env]
inherit = true                     # default true. false = hermetic env.
[env.extra]                        # merged on top
LOG_LEVEL = "info"
PYTHONUNBUFFERED = "1"

# ─── [defaults] — agent-wide retry/backoff (optional) ─────────────────
[defaults]
max_retries = 3                    # 0 = no retry
retry_backoff_minutes = [5, 15, 30]
stale_after_minutes = 120          # window older than this → state=stale

# ─── [[schedules]] — at least one, UNLESS trigger-only ────────────────
# An agent that only ever runs because something asked (a Telegram message,
# a local client, or an MCP tools/call) may declare zero schedules. dotagent gives
# it the synthetic schedule id "trigger". See section 19.
[[schedules]]
id = "daily"                       # REQUIRED. Unique within manifest.
type = "cron"                      # "cron" | "interval" | "expression"
weekdays = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]         # 0=Sun..6=Sat. cron only.
hours = [8]                        # cron only. Any of 0..23.
minute = 30                        # cron only. 0..59.
args = ["--period", "yesterday"]   # appended to [run].args
# Per-schedule overrides (override [defaults] above):
max_retries = 20
retry_backoff_minutes = [30]
stale_after_minutes = 240
on_battery = "defer"               # "run" (default) | "defer" — overrides
                                   # [power] in config.toml for this schedule

[[schedules]]
id = "every-90"
type = "interval"
interval_minutes = 90              # interval only.

[[schedules]]
id = "linux-only"
type = "expression"
expression = "Mon..Fri *-*-* 08:00:00"  # systemd OnCalendar format (NOT cron syntax!)

# ─── [[preflight]] — abort the run if any check fails (optional) ──────
[[preflight]]
plugin = "preflight-warp"
config = { connect_command = "warp-cli connect" }

# ─── [[notifiers]] — built-in, in-process (optional) ──────────────────
[[notifiers]]
driver = "imessage"                # built-in driver names below
to = "+5511999999999"
rate_limit_minutes = 60
events = ["given_up"]              # empty / absent = all events

# ─── [[on_success]] / [[on_failure]] — plugin hooks (optional) ────────
[[on_success]]
plugin = "sink-file"
config = { path = "/Users/me/reports/today.md", mode = "overwrite" }

# ─── [security] — declared intent, schema-only in v0 (optional) ───────
[security]
allowed_commands = ["python3", "/usr/bin/python3"]
allowed_plugins = ["preflight-warp", "sink-roam"]
network = "allow"                  # "allow" | "deny" | ["host1", "host2"]
filesystem_writable = ["/Users/me/reports"]
env_passthrough = ["PATH", "HOME", "LANG"]
```

### Field-by-field quick reference

| Block          | Field                  | Type            | Required | Default                |
|----------------|------------------------|-----------------|----------|------------------------|
| `[agent]`      | `name`                 | string          | yes      | —                      |
| `[agent]`      | `description`          | string          | no       | —                      |
| `[agent]`      | `monitor`              | bool            | no       | `true`                 |
| `[agent]`      | `timeout_seconds`      | int             | no       | `1800`                 |
| `[run]`        | `command`              | string          | yes      | —                      |
| `[run]`        | `args`                 | `string[]`      | no       | `[]`                   |
| `[run]`        | `working_dir`          | string          | no       | manifest dir           |
| `[run]`        | `protocol`             | string          | no      | absent (plain stdout)  |
| `[env]`        | `inherit`              | bool            | no       | `true`                 |
| `[env.extra]`  | (any key)              | string          | no       | —                      |
| `[defaults]`   | `max_retries`          | int             | no       | `0`                    |
| `[defaults]`   | `retry_backoff_minutes`| `int[]`         | no       | `[]`                   |
| `[defaults]`   | `stale_after_minutes`  | int             | no       | (no stale check)       |
| `[[schedules]]`| `id`                   | string          | yes      | —                      |
| `[[schedules]]`| `type`                 | `"cron"`/`"interval"`/`"expression"` | yes | —      |
| `[[schedules]]`| `weekdays`             | `int[]` (0..6)  | cron     | (any)                  |
| `[[schedules]]`| `hours`                | `int[]` (0..23) | cron     | (any)                  |
| `[[schedules]]`| `minute`               | int (0..59)     | cron     | `0`                    |
| `[[schedules]]`| `interval_minutes`     | int             | interval | —                      |
| `[[schedules]]`| `expression`           | string          | expr     | — (systemd OnCalendar) |
| `[[schedules]]`| `args`                 | `string[]`      | no       | `[]`                   |
| `[[schedules]]`| `on_battery`           | `run`/`defer`   | no       | `[power] on_battery`   |
| `[lifecycle]`  | `mode`                 | `oneshot`/`persistent` | no | `oneshot`           |
| `[lifecycle]`  | `key`                  | string          | no       | — (single instance)    |
| `[lifecycle]`  | `idle_timeout_seconds` | int             | no       | `1800`                 |
| `[lifecycle]`  | `max_invocations`      | int             | no       | `120` (`0` = unlimited)|
| `[lifecycle]`  | `max_instances`        | int             | no       | `8`                    |
| `[lifecycle]`  | `startup_timeout_seconds` | int          | no       | `30`                   |
| `[[preflight]]`| `plugin`               | string          | yes      | —                      |
| `[[preflight]]`| `config`               | table           | no       | `{}`                   |
| `[[preflight]]`| `timeout_seconds`      | int             | no       | `30`                   |
| `[[notifiers]]`| `driver`               | string          | yes      | —                      |
| `[[notifiers]]`| `events`               | `string[]`      | no       | (all events)           |
| `[[notifiers]]`| (driver-specific)      | varies          | varies   | varies                 |
| `[[on_success]]`/`[[on_failure]]` | `plugin`           | string     | yes | —                |
| `[[on_success]]`/`[[on_failure]]` | `config`           | table      | no  | `{}`             |
| `[[on_success]]`/`[[on_failure]]` | `events`           | `string[]` | no  | (all events)     |
| `[[on_success]]`/`[[on_failure]]` | `timeout_seconds`  | int        | no  | `300` / `15`     |

---

## 4. Environment variables dotagent injects

When the daemon spawns your agent, these `AGENT_*` vars are set on top
of the inherited parent env (unless `env.inherit = false`).

| Variable               | Type        | Example                                            |
|------------------------|-------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `AGENT_NAME`           | string      | `finops-weekly`                                    |
| `AGENT_HOME`           | abs path    | `/Users/me/.config/dotagent/agents/finops-weekly`  |
| `AGENT_TMPDIR`         | abs path    | `/var/folders/.../tmpAbCdEf` (auto-cleaned on exit)|
| `AGENT_DRY_RUN`        | `"true"`/`"false"` | `"false"`                                   |
| `AGENT_SCHEDULE_ID`    | string      | `daily`                                            |
| `AGENT_SLUG`           | string      | `period_yesterday` (derived from schedule args)    |
| `AGENT_START_EPOCH`    | int         | `1700000000`                                       |
| `AGENT_ARGV`           | JSON array  | `["--period","yesterday"]`                         |
| `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE` | abs path    | (empty when `AGENT_DRY_RUN=true`)                  |

> **Important**: `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE` is **read-only from the agent's
> perspective**. dotagent writes the heartbeat before and after the run.
> Do NOT have your agent write to that path — you'll race with the
> daemon. If you need to persist arbitrary state, use `AGENT_HOME` or
> a sink plugin.

Runs started by a **trigger** (a Telegram message, a local client message, or
an MCP `tools/call`) instead of a schedule get additional context. They are applied BEFORE the block
above, so a payload can never redefine `AGENT_NAME` or
`AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`.

| Variable                 | Type   | Example                                    |
|--------------------------|--------|--------------------------------------------|
| `AGENT_TRIGGER_SOURCE`   | string | `telegram` \| `local` \| `mcp` \| `cli`     |
| `AGENT_TRIGGER_ACTOR`    | string | `123456789` (Telegram numeric user id)     |
| `AGENT_TRIGGER_REPLY_TO` | string | `123456789` (chat id to answer)            |
| `AGENT_TRIGGER_PAYLOAD`  | JSON   | `{"text":"sim","chat_id":1,"user_id":2,"message_id":9,"reply_to_text":"Posso criar?"}` |
| `AGENT_SESSION_ID`       | string | `chat-9_a` (opaque conversation key)      |

When the sender invoked a command, the payload also carries
`{"command":{"name":"standup","args":"disk-alert"}}` — the resolved catalog
name, ready to pass to `command-get`. It is `null` for ordinary prose.

A **persistent** agent gets none of those per-message values (see §19b): the environment
is fixed at spawn and that process answers many messages, so the trigger
rides in each request frame instead. It gets `AGENT_LIFECYCLE=persistent`
and `AGENT_PERSIST_KEY=<key>`, and its `AGENT_TMPDIR` survives between
requests rather than being fresh per run.

The message body travels in `AGENT_TRIGGER_PAYLOAD`, never in argv.
When the sender used Telegram's reply, `reply_to_text` carries what they
replied to — a bare "sim" is meaningless without it.
Whatever a triggered agent prints on stdout is sent back to whoever
asked; log to stderr.

`AGENT_SESSION_ID` is opaque and belongs to the trigger source. The daemon does
not persist a transcript or LLM session; the agent decides how to use the key.
The local API validates it as `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` and defaults an omitted id
to `default`.

### Slug derivation

`AGENT_SLUG` comes from the schedule's `args`:

| args                          | slug                  |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------|
| `[]`                          | `default`             |
| `["--period", "yesterday"]`   | `period_yesterday`    |
| `["--mode", "unsubscribe"]`   | `mode_unsubscribe`    |
| `["foo bar"]`                 | `foo_bar`             |

Rules: strip leading dashes, lowercase, replace non-alphanumeric with
`_`, collapse repeated `_`, trim trailing `_`. Empty → `default`.

For triggered runs, the slug is `trigger-<source>` without a session and
`trigger-<source>-<sanitized-session>` with one. A local API request that omits
`session_id` uses its effective `default` session and therefore writes
`trigger-local-default`.

### Reading env vars

```fish
echo "$AGENT_NAME ran with schedule $AGENT_SCHEDULE_ID"
test "$AGENT_DRY_RUN" = "true"; and exit 0
cd $AGENT_TMPDIR
```

```python
import os, json
name = os.environ["AGENT_NAME"]
argv = json.loads(os.environ.get("AGENT_ARGV", "[]"))
if os.environ.get("AGENT_DRY_RUN") == "true":
    exit(0)
```

```go
name := os.Getenv("AGENT_NAME")
var argv []string
json.Unmarshal([]byte(os.Getenv("AGENT_ARGV")), &argv)
```

```bash
: "${AGENT_NAME:?running outside dotagent?}"
cd "$AGENT_TMPDIR" || exit
```

---

## 5. Schedules

Three types. A **single** daemon owns all of them — there is no per-agent
plist and no per-agent systemd timer. launchd / systemd start the daemon;
the daemon computes the next event across every schedule and sleeps to it.

### `type = "cron"`

A window is due when `weekday matches AND hour matches AND minute matches`.

```toml
[[schedules]]
id = "daily-weekdays-8am"
type = "cron"
weekdays = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]   # Mon..Fri (0=Sun..6=Sat)
hours = [8]
minute = 30                  # daily at 08:30 Mon..Fri
```

```toml
[[schedules]]
id = "twice-a-day"
type = "cron"
hours = [9, 18]              # any weekday
minute = 0                   # daily at 09:00 and 18:00
```

### `type = "interval"`

An arithmetic sequence of ticks anchored on the last **success**
(`last_success`, `+iv`, `+2·iv`, …); the window due now is the greatest tick
`<= now`. A success re-phases the sequence.

The sequence keeps advancing **while runs fail**, like the calendar keeps
producing cron windows. A frozen `last_success + iv` window would age past
`stale_after_minutes`, get skipped on every tick, never advance `last_success`,
and deadlock the agent permanently (one real case: 55 days dead).

Staleness is judged against the **first missed** window, not the rolling one —
otherwise a chronically failing agent reads as a fresh failure forever.

`interval_minutes` must be greater than zero; manifest validation rejects `0`
before the schedule reaches the scheduler.

```toml
[[schedules]]
id = "every-90-min"
type = "interval"
interval_minutes = 90
```

### `type = "expression"` — **not implemented yet**

> The manifest field parses and validates, but the scheduler has no
> expression parser: `expected_at` and `compute_next_event` both return
> `None` for it, so the schedule **never comes due**. Use `cron` or
> `interval`. This section documents the intended syntax only.

Free-form systemd `OnCalendar` syntax. **NOT cron syntax** — this is
systemd's calendar event format.

```toml
[[schedules]]
id = "linux-weekdays-9am"
type = "expression"
expression = "Mon..Fri *-*-* 09:00:00"   # systemd OnCalendar
```

Quick `OnCalendar` examples:
- `*-*-* 08:00:00` — daily at 08:00
- `Mon..Fri *-*-* 08:30:00` — weekdays at 08:30
- `*-*-01 09:00:00` — first day of each month at 09:00
- `*-*-* *:00:00` — every hour on the hour
- `Mon *-*-* 09:00:00` — every Monday at 09:00

If you want cross-platform, **use `cron` or `interval`**, not `expression`.

---

## 6. Notifier drivers (built-in, in-process)

Drivers live inside the daemon (crate `dotagent-notify`). No subprocess
fork, no extra binaries on `$PATH`.

| Driver     | Transport                                | Subprocess?            |
|------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------|
| `desktop`  | `NSUserNotification` / D-Bus             | No                     |
| `slack`    | HTTPS POST to Slack Incoming Webhooks    | No                     |
| `ntfy`     | HTTPS POST to ntfy.sh (or self-hosted)   | No                     |
| `pushover` | HTTPS POST to api.pushover.net           | No                     |
| `telegram` | HTTPS POST to api.telegram.org (Bot API)  | No                    |
| `imessage` | `osascript` Messages.app automation      | **Yes** (no Apple API) |
| `plugin`   | Escape hatch → plugin protocol           | Yes                    |

### Credentials: use `${VAR}`, never a literal

An `agent.toml` is a versioned file. Every credential-bearing field accepts
`${VAR}`, resolved **at send time** against `~/.config/dotagent/secrets.env`
first, then `std::env::var`:

| Driver     | `${VAR}`-expanded                     | Left literal (address, not secret) |
|------------|---------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| `slack`    | `webhook_url`                         | —                                  |
| `ntfy`     | `token`, `base_url`, `topic`          | —                                  |
| `pushover` | `token`, `user`                       | —                                  |
| `telegram` | `bot_token`                           | `chat_id`                          |
| `imessage` | —                                     | `to`                               |

An unresolved reference **fails the send** — no fall-through to the literal
`${…}` string. The error names only the field and the variable.

Transport errors never carry the URL: `NotifyError` has no
`From<reqwest::Error>`, because `reqwest`'s `Display` appends ` for url (…)`
and for Slack/Telegram that URL is the credential.

### Message size caps (body is trimmed, not dropped)

| Driver     | Body              | Title            |
|------------|-------------------|------------------|
| `slack`    | 40,000 chars      | —                |
| `telegram` | 4,096 chars       | —                |
| `pushover` | 1,024 chars       | 250 chars        |
| `ntfy`     | 4,096 **bytes**   | 250 **bytes**    |

Over-limit bodies are cut with a `[truncated]` marker (`…` on titles) rather
than rejected by the backend. ntfy counts **bytes**: `ç`/`ã` are 2 bytes, an
emoji is 4, so a char-based trim can ship 4× the limit.

### `desktop`

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "desktop"
title = "my-agent"          # default: agent name
subtitle = "free space low" # macOS only
sound = true                # macOS only
urgency = "critical"        # Linux only: low | normal | critical
icon = "dialog-warning"     # Linux only: icon name or absolute path
expire_ms = 5000            # Linux only: 0 = persistent
events = ["given_up"]
```

### `slack`

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "slack"
webhook_url = "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}"   # the URL *is* the credential
channel = "#alerts"         # optional
username = "dotagent"       # optional
icon_emoji = ":robot_face:" # optional
events = ["given_up", "recovered"]
```

### `ntfy`

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "ntfy"
topic = "${NTFY_TOPIC}"        # on public ntfy.sh the topic name is the secret
base_url = "https://ntfy.sh"   # default; self-host friendly
token = "${NTFY_TOKEN}"        # optional bearer auth
priority = 4                   # 1..5
title = "disk-alert"           # default: agent name
tags = ["warning", "skull"]
events = ["given_up"]
```

### `pushover`

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "pushover"
token = "${PUSHOVER_TOKEN}"
user  = "${PUSHOVER_USER}"
priority = 1
title = "disk-alert"           # default: agent name
events = ["given_up"]
```

### `telegram`

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "telegram"
bot_token = "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"
chat_id = "-1001234567890"       # or "@my_channel". NOT ${VAR}-expanded.
parse_mode = "MarkdownV2"        # optional: MarkdownV2 | HTML | Markdown
disable_notification = false     # optional
events = ["given_up"]
```

With `parse_mode = "MarkdownV2"` dotagent escapes the **19** reserved
characters (``\_*[]()~`>#+-=|{}.!`` — backslash included). The body **always**
goes through the escaper, so pre-escaping doubles the backslashes; use
`parse_mode = "HTML"` if you need live markup. Escaping runs before the 4096
cut (it grows the text), and a backslash orphaned by the cut is dropped —
Telegram rejects the whole message over one dangling escape.

API refusals log the Bot API's own `description`, with the token scrubbed.

### `imessage` (macOS only)

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "imessage"
to = "+5511999999999"            # phone or email iMessage handle
rate_limit_minutes = 60          # skip-if-recent; 0 disables
events = ["given_up"]
```

### `plugin` (escape hatch for third-party notifiers)

```toml
[[notifiers]]
driver = "plugin"
name = "notify-discord"          # plugin binary: dotagent-plugin-notify-discord
events = ["given_up"]
[notifiers.config]
webhook_url = "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/..."
```

---

## 7. Built-in plugins (preflight + sink)

Plugins are external binaries (`dotagent-plugin-<name>`) speaking JSON
over stdio. The dotagent install (via Homebrew or release tarball)
ships these five first-party plugins.

### `preflight-warp` — abort if Cloudflare WARP is disconnected

```toml
[[preflight]]
plugin = "preflight-warp"
config = { connect_command = "warp-cli connect" }  # optional hint shown in failure notification
# Optional: { binary = "/usr/local/bin/warp-cli" }
```

### `preflight-cmd` — abort if a command fails

```toml
[[preflight]]
plugin = "preflight-cmd"
config = {
  command = "gh",
  args = ["auth", "status"],
  expect_exit = 0,                # default 0
  expect_contains = "Logged in"   # optional substring in stdout/stderr
}
```

### `sink-file` — write agent stdout to a file

```toml
[[on_success]]
plugin = "sink-file"
config = { path = "/Users/me/reports/today.md", mode = "overwrite" }
# mode: "overwrite" (default) | "append"
```

### `sink-roam` — publish agent stdout to a Roam page (via `mcp` CLI)

```toml
[[on_success]]
plugin = "sink-roam"
config = {
  page = "today",                        # or "April 22nd, 2026" or "acme/tech/aws/X"
  marker_regex = "#DORA.*yesterday",     # idempotent replace (deletes match, re-creates)
  mcp_binary = "~/.cargo/bin/mcp"        # default
}
```

Roam-specific: `page` accepts `today` (resolves to current daily note),
a named daily in **ordinal format** (`April 22nd, 2026` — not ISO!), or
a namespaced page path (`acme/tech/aws/finops-2026`, created if missing).

Stdin expected format (parsed as hierarchy):

```
#TAG First line is ROOT (no indentation)
  L1 header — direct child (indent ≤ 3 spaces)
    L2 child of previous L1 (indent > 3 spaces)
  Another L1
    L2 of that L1
---
Notes after `---` separator are cut.
```

### `sink-outl` — publish agent stdout to an Outl page (via `mcp` CLI)

Twin of `sink-roam` with identical config shape. Internally uses
`outl_batch` so the delete + write happens in a single round-trip.

```toml
[[on_success]]
plugin = "sink-outl"
config = {
  page = "today",                        # or "2026-06-01" / "April 22nd, 2026" / "acme/tech/aws"
  marker_regex = "#DORA.*yesterday",     # idempotent replace (deletes match, re-creates)
  mcp_binary = "~/.cargo/bin/mcp"        # default
}
```

Outl-specific: daily slug is **ISO** (`2026-06-01`); the plugin also
accepts Roam's ordinal form and normalizes it. Same stdin hierarchy
convention as `sink-roam` (root + L1/L2, fences stripped, `---` cuts).

---

## 8. Events

| Event           | Fires when                                          |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `attempt_failed`| Run exited non-zero (a retry may still happen)      |
| `timed_out`     | Run exceeded `agent.timeout_seconds`                |
| `given_up`      | All retries exhausted — repeats while it stays true  |
| `stale`         | Schedule stopped running at all (window aged out)    |
| `recovered`     | A previously-failing schedule passed                 |
| `success`       | Every successful run (use sparingly — noisy)         |
| `preflight`     | A preflight plugin returned `ok: false`              |
| `daily_summary` | Daily health roll-up at `[daily_summary].time` (22:45)|

`[[notifiers]]` and `[[on_*]]` accept `events = [...]` to filter. Empty
or absent = all events.

`daily_summary` is the exception: it is the daemon's event, not an
agent's, and only reaches `[[daily_summary.notifiers]]` in
`config.toml`. Listing it in a manifest matches nothing.

```toml
# ~/.config/dotagent/config.toml — all defaults shown
[daily_summary]
enabled       = true      # governs the daemon's fire, not `dotagent daily-summary`
time          = "22:45"   # local HH:MM; unparseable falls back here, never off
grace_minutes = 30        # clamped to [1, 1440]

[[daily_summary.notifiers]]   # none declared = `desktop`
driver    = "telegram"
bot_token = "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"
chat_id   = "123456789"
```

The daemon schedules its own wake-up for `time`. `events` inside those
entries is ignored — the list is already scoped to one event.

Power policy lives in the same file. Defaults change nothing; the probe
(`pmset` on macOS, `/sys/class/power_supply` on Linux) does not even run
unless one of the two fields can defer something. An undetectable power
source reads as mains — a machine whose battery cannot be read must keep
running its agents.

```toml
# ~/.config/dotagent/config.toml — all defaults shown
[power]
on_battery          = "run"   # "run" | "defer" — defer holds runs until AC
min_battery_percent = 0       # defer below this charge, whatever the above says
```

Deferring does not queue: both schedule kinds resolve to the *current*
window, so an agent deferred across four hours of battery runs once when
the charger goes in, not sixteen times. A deferred run writes no window
state and burns no retry. The check is after the staleness check, so a
window that ages past `stale_after_minutes` while unplugged is dropped.

`stale` and `given_up` fire from a *condition*, not a one-off event, so they
re-notify on a rising ladder — on entry, then 1h, 6h, daily — until the
schedule succeeds again. State lives in `state/notify/alerts.json` and survives
daemon restarts. `stale` is delivered on the `given_up` channel when no entry
lists it explicitly, so an existing `events = ["given_up"]` needs no edit.

---

## 9. Exit code semantics

dotagent only cares about **zero vs non-zero**.

| Exit code      | Meaning                              | Event fired       |
|----------------|--------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `0`            | Success                              | `success` (+ `recovered` if previously failing) |
| any non-zero   | Failure attempt                      | `attempt_failed`  |
| (SIGKILL by daemon) | Exceeded `timeout_seconds`      | `timed_out`       |

There's no special handling for `2`, `127`, etc. If you want to surface
the *kind* of failure to a sink/notifier, write a structured line to
stderr — dotagent captures the last 5 stderr lines into the failure
message.

---

## 10. Heartbeat shape

dotagent writes a heartbeat file before AND after every non-dry-run
execution. Your agent should treat this as **read-only**:

```
~/.config/dotagent/state/agents/{name}/{slug}.heartbeat.json
```

Shape (read this if you want to query history from another agent):

```jsonc
{
  "name": "my-agent",
  "slug": "default",
  "args": [],
  "started_at": 1700000000,
  "started_at_iso": "2023-11-14T22:13:20+0000",
  "finished_at": 1700000100,
  "finished_at_iso": "2023-11-14T22:15:00+0000",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "duration_seconds": 100,
  "last_success_at": 1700000100,         // preserved; never overwritten on failure
  "last_success_at_iso": "2023-11-14T22:15:00+0000"
}
```

---

## 11. Health states

Computed per `(agent, schedule)` pair on every `tick`:

| State     | Meaning                                                                       |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `ok`      | `last_success_at >= expected_at` and no retries needed                        |
| `degraded`| The window succeeded, but only after ≥1 **failed** attempt                     |
| `failing` | Window passed without success; retrying or already given up                   |
| `stale`   | Never ran, OR window older than `stale_after_minutes`                         |

---

## 12. Common `dotagent doctor` errors

| Error message                                  | Cause                                                    |
|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `agent name missing`                           | `[agent].name` not set                                   |
| `agent name not unique`                        | Two manifests claim the same `name`                      |
| `at least one [[schedules]] required`          | Retired: trigger-only manifests may omit schedules        |
| `schedule id missing`                          | `[[schedules]].id` not set                               |
| `schedule id not unique within manifest`       | Two schedules share the same `id`                        |
| `weekdays out of range`                        | A value in `weekdays` is not in `0..=6`                  |
| `hours out of range`                           | A value in `hours` is not in `0..=23`                    |
| `minute out of range`                          | `minute` not in `0..=59`                                 |
| `interval_minutes required for type=interval`  | Missing field on interval schedule                       |
| `expression required for type=expression`      | Missing field on expression schedule                     |
| `expression type only supported on Linux`      | Used `expression` on macOS                               |
| `command missing`                              | `[run].command` not set                                  |
| `unknown notifier driver`                      | `[[notifiers]].driver` is not one of the 6 valid values  |
| `notifier slack: webhook_url required`         | (driver-specific required field)                         |
| `plugin <name> not found on $PATH`             | The plugin binary isn't installed                        |
| `⚠ no [security] section`                      | Harmless warning; v0 is schema-only                      |

---

## 13. Complete examples (combining features)

### Example A — Python agent, cron weekday, Slack notifier, preflight + sink

```toml
# ~/.config/dotagent/agents/team-standup/agent.toml
[agent]
name = "team-standup"
description = "Daily team summary from GitHub + Sentry, posted to Slack and Roam."
timeout_seconds = 600

[run]
command = "uv"
args = ["run", "./agent.py"]

[env.extra]
LOG_LEVEL = "info"

[defaults]
max_retries = 5
retry_backoff_minutes = [10, 20, 40, 80, 160]
stale_after_minutes = 240

[[schedules]]
id = "daily"
type = "cron"
weekdays = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]   # Mon..Fri
hours = [8]
minute = 30

# Don't run if VPN is down — retries will keep trying every backoff.
[[preflight]]
plugin = "preflight-warp"
config = { connect_command = "warp-cli connect" }

# Tier 1: noisy desktop banner on every failed attempt
[[notifiers]]
driver = "desktop"
title = "team-standup"
events = ["attempt_failed", "given_up"]

# Tier 2: Slack only after retries exhausted
[[notifiers]]
driver = "slack"
webhook_url = "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}"   # value lives in secrets.env
channel = "#eng-ops"
events = ["given_up", "recovered"]

# Persist the rendered output to today's Roam daily note
[[on_success]]
plugin = "sink-roam"
config = { page = "today", marker_regex = "#STANDUP.*\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}" }

[security]
allowed_commands = ["uv", "python3"]
allowed_plugins  = ["preflight-warp", "sink-roam"]
network          = ["api.github.com", "acme.sentry.io", "hooks.slack.com"]
filesystem_writable = []
env_passthrough  = ["PATH", "HOME", "GITHUB_TOKEN", "SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN"]
```

### Example B — Go binary, interval, iMessage on give-up

```toml
# ~/.config/dotagent/agents/disk-alert/agent.toml
[agent]
name = "disk-alert"
description = "Alert when free space on / drops below threshold."
timeout_seconds = 30

[run]
command = "./agent"          # compiled Go binary in the agent dir

[env.extra]
DISK_FREE_MIN_PCT = "20"
DISK_CHECK_MOUNT = "/"

[defaults]
max_retries = 3
retry_backoff_minutes = [5, 15, 30]
stale_after_minutes = 120

[[schedules]]
id = "every-15min"
type = "interval"
interval_minutes = 15

[[notifiers]]
driver = "desktop"
title = "disk-alert"
subtitle = "free space low"
sound = true
urgency = "critical"
events = ["attempt_failed", "given_up"]

[[notifiers]]
driver = "imessage"
to = "+5511999999999"
rate_limit_minutes = 60        # at most 1 ping/hour even on extended failure
events = ["given_up"]
```

### Example C — Pure shell collector, daily, file sink only

```toml
# ~/.config/dotagent/agents/hn-morning/agent.toml
[agent]
name = "hn-morning"
description = "Top 5 HN stories at 08:00 weekdays."
timeout_seconds = 60

[run]
command = "fish"
args = ["./agent.fish"]

[[schedules]]
id = "weekdays-8am"
type = "cron"
weekdays = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
hours = [8]
minute = 0

[[on_success]]
plugin = "sink-file"
config = { path = "/Users/me/reports/hn-today.md", mode = "overwrite" }
```

---

## 14. What dotagent does NOT do

- **Run your business logic.** It's a scheduler + supervisor.
- **Provide an SDK.** Read env vars, write stdout/stderr, exit. That's
  the entire API surface.
- **Register one OS timer per schedule.** launchd / systemd start the
  single daemon; the daemon computes the next event across all schedules
  and sleeps to it.
- **Substitute the `mcp` CLI.** `sink-roam` calls `mcp` separately.
- **Run on Windows.** Linux + WSL works; native Windows doesn't.
- **Template `path` or any config field.** No `{{vars}}` — your agent
  must build dynamic paths itself.

---

## 15. Filesystem layout

```
~/.config/dotagent/
├── agents/<name>/agent.toml         # manifests
├── state/
│   ├── agents/<name>/<slug>.heartbeat.json
│   ├── windows/<name>-<slug>-<ts>.json   # swept: [state] window_retention_days (30)
│   ├── notify/alerts.json           # re-notification ladder for ongoing alerts
│   ├── known_manifests.json
│   └── daemon.pid
├── logs/
│   ├── daemon/dotagent.log          # daemon tracing (JSON, rotated daily)
│   ├── daemon/run.avelino.dotagent.log        # launchd/systemd stdout
│   ├── daemon/run.avelino.dotagent-error.log  # stderr — CRASHES ONLY
│   └── agents/<name>/<name>.log     # rotated; per-agent
├── audit.log                        # JSONL audit trail (live)
├── audit.log.20260806T101500        # sealed segment, never auto-deleted
├── secrets.env                      # optional, mode 0600
├── config.toml                      # optional dotagent config
└── api.sock                         # local UDS API when dispatcher is discovered
```

Retention notes:

- `audit.log` rotates at **32MB** into `audit.log.<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>`, stitched
  by an `audit_log_rotated` **seam** whose `prev_hash` is the old segment's
  tail hash — the chain crosses the rename. Segments are never deleted
  automatically.
- `tick_started` / `tick_completed` are **no longer emitted** (they were 64% of
  the file). The enum variants remain so old logs still parse.
- The log sweeper never touches the **active** file — launchd/systemd hold an
  open fd on it.
- `state/windows/` is the only unbounded state dir; the 03:00 sweep applies
  `[state] window_retention_days` (default 30, `0` disables).

Discovery order for manifests:

1. Every directory in `$DOTAGENT_ROOT` (colon-separated)
2. `$DOTAGENT_HOME/agents/` (default `~/.config/dotagent/agents/`)
3. `$CWD/agents/`
4. `$CWD`

Discovery order for plugin binaries:

1. Every directory in `$DOTAGENT_PLUGIN_PATH`
2. `$DOTAGENT_HOME/plugins/`
3. `/usr/local/lib/dotagent/plugins/`
4. `$PATH`

---

## 16. Env vars dotagent reads (overrides)

| Variable                       | Purpose                                                              | Default              |
|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| `DOTAGENT_HOME`                | Root directory                                                       | `~/.config/dotagent` |
| `DOTAGENT_ROOT`                | Extra manifest search dirs (colon-separated), prepended to default   | (empty)              |
| `DOTAGENT_PLUGIN_PATH`         | Extra plugin search dirs (colon-separated), prepended to default     | (empty)              |
| `RUST_LOG`                     | Tracing filter; overrides `[logging].level` in `config.toml`         | `info`               |
| `DOTAGENT_LOG_STDERR`          | Force the stderr mirror on (`1`/`true`/`yes`/`on`) or off (`0`/`false`/`no`/`off`) | (mirror follows TTY) |
| `NO_COLOR`                     | Any value suppresses ANSI in the daemon and every subcommand         | (unset)              |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`   | OTLP auth headers (comma-separated `k=v`); used when OTLP enabled    | (empty)              |

The daemon mirrors `tracing` to stderr **only when stderr is a TTY**. Under
launchd / systemd stderr is an unrotated file, so `…-error.log` receives
crashes only — read `logs/daemon/dotagent.log` for activity.

---

## 17. CLI surface (most common)

```bash
dotagent doctor                  # validate every manifest discoverable
dotagent run <name>              # foreground run for smoke-testing
dotagent run <name> --schedule <id> --dry-run
dotagent status                  # health dashboard
dotagent logs <name> --follow    # tail an agent's log
dotagent tick                    # what would the daemon do right now?
dotagent reload                  # SIGHUP daemon — picks up manifest changes
dotagent install                 # write launchd plist / systemd unit
dotagent uninstall               # remove launchd plist / systemd unit
dotagent plugin list             # list resolved plugin binaries
dotagent inspect <name>          # heartbeat + windows + schedule resolution
dotagent daily-summary           # ad-hoc daily roll-up
dotagent run-now <name>          # force a run now, ignoring schedule windows
dotagent mcp                     # serve every agent as an MCP tool over stdio
dotagent api                     # raw JSONL bridge to the daemon's local API socket
dotagent audit verify --full     # verify the audit log's hash chain; exits 1 on a break
dotagent completions <shell>     # bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell — tab-completes agent names
```

---

## 18. Patterns (pick the closest shape)

| Pattern                | Shape                                                                | When to use                              |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Pure data collector    | APIs → jq/filter → sink                                              | Output is structured data, no LLM needed |
| Brief / digest         | Sources → LLM (cheap model) → notifier                               | Input is noisy, want 3 bullets           |
| Triage / classifier    | Source → heuristic for 80% → LLM for residue → apply labels          | Mostly deterministic, LLM for the tail   |
| Generator + idempotent | Sources → LLM → sink with `marker_regex` (replace, don't append)     | Re-runs shouldn't duplicate              |
| Watchdog / preflight   | `preflight-cmd` or `preflight-warp` → empty agent body → notifier    | Just want to alert on a condition        |

---

## 19. Triggers — runs caused by an event, not the clock

A run can start because something asked: a Telegram message arrived, a local
client sent a message, or an MCP client called a tool. A triggered run keeps everything a scheduled
one has (supervisor, heartbeat, audit, hooks, notifiers) and differs in
two ways: it has **no window state** (no attempts counter, never
consumes a retry, never marks a cron window given up) and it uses its
**own slug** (`trigger-<source>`, or `trigger-<source>-<sanitized-session>`
when a session is present) so it can't overwrite
`last_success_at` for a window that never fired.

Triggers enter a gateway with one FIFO worker per conversation key
`(source, session_id/reply_to/default)`. Same-conversation order is preserved;
different conversations run in parallel up to a default cap of four. This is
**not** serialized against the scheduler's tick. A long scheduled run no longer
delays a chat reply; a long triggered run still delays the next trigger for its
conversation. The gateway and per-conversation queues are bounded at 64 pending
jobs, then apply backpressure.

### MCP server — every agent as a tool

```bash
dotagent mcp     # JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, one object per line
```

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "dotagent": { "command": "dotagent", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

Methods: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, `ping`. One tool per
discovered agent, named `run-<sanitized-agent-name>`. Tool description
comes from `agent.description` — write a good one, it's what a model
uses to choose. Arguments: `{"schedule": "daily", "args": ["--flag"]}`,
both optional.

An agent that FAILS returns a normal result with `isError: true` and the
exit code in the text, NOT a JSON-RPC error. JSON-RPC errors mean
protocol faults (unknown method, unknown tool, bad params).

Agents run in the `dotagent mcp` process, like `run-now` — not through
the daemon — so they don't appear in `dotagent status`.

### Memory — facts that outlive the conversation

`dotagent mcp` also exposes `memory-remember` and `memory-recall`,
backed by an embedded outl workspace at `~/.config/dotagent/outl`
(scaffolded on daemon start; override with `[memory] workspace`).

Memory is NOT conversation history. History is what was just said;
memory is what stays true next week — a preference, a decision, a
correction.

It is a graph. `memory-remember` takes `text` + `topics[]`; each topic
becomes a `[[link]]` to a page, and outl's backlinks make that page
gather every fact mentioning it. So one fact, stored once in the day's
journal, is reachable both by date and by subject.

- `memory-remember {text, topics[]}` — store, linked
- `memory-recall {topic}` — everything linked to a subject (ask the graph)
- `memory-recall {query}` — substring search (fallback, not semantic)
- `memory-topics {}` — what subjects exist; check before inventing a name

Reuse topic names. `dotagent` and `dot-agent` are two disconnected pages
about the same thing, and both look incomplete.

Do not store what is already in the conversation, or anything the agent
can look up on demand. A memory store full of noise makes recall return
the wrong thing.

Turn off with `[memory] enabled = false`.

### Telegram ingress — talk to your agents from a chat

Daemon-level config, NOT per-manifest (Telegram allows one `getUpdates`
consumer per bot token):

```toml
# ~/.config/dotagent/config.toml
[telegram]
bot_token        = "${TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}"
allowed_user_ids = [123456789]     # numeric ids; EMPTY MEANS NOBODY
dispatcher_agent = "telegram-assistant"
```

Off unless both `bot_token` and a non-empty `allowed_user_ids` are set.
An empty allowlist is treated as misconfiguration, not as "allow
everyone" — the other reading turns a typo into an open
remote-execution endpoint.

Every accepted message runs `dispatcher_agent` with the body in
`AGENT_TRIGGER_PAYLOAD`; that agent's stdout is sent back to the chat.
The dispatcher is an ordinary agent — dotagent interprets nothing and
there is no model in the daemon.

Security: this is the one path where someone with NO access to the
machine can cause a local process to run. Read V8 in
`docs/security/threat-model.md` before enabling.

### Local client API — same-machine assistant transport

When `telegram.dispatcher_agent` resolves to a discovered agent, the daemon
also listens on `$DOTAGENT_HOME/api.sock` (default
`~/.config/dotagent/api.sock`) with Unix-socket permissions `0600`. This is
JSON Lines, not HTTP/TCP, and is independent of whether Telegram polling has a
bot token and allowlist.

Requests are `message.send` (`{"session_id?":"...","text":"..."}`),
`commands.list`, and `status.get`. Responses are `{id,result}` or
`{id,error}`; ids may be strings or numbers and are normalized to strings.
Events are `typing`, `run.started`, raw `reply.delta`, and final `reply`.
The socket caps connections at 16, requests at 30/minute/connection, text at
32 KiB, session ids at 64 ASCII identifier characters, and pending event bytes
at 1 MiB. A slow client is disconnected.

The API is a harness boundary: it routes and supervises the configured
dispatcher, but it does not own sessions, transcripts, or LLM state. Local
clients receive raw streaming deltas; Telegram remains final-only. Full wire
contract: `docs/reference/local-api.md`.

### A broken manifest does not stop the others

An `agent.toml` that fails to parse or validate is skipped, reported by
`dotagent doctor`, and audited as `manifest_invalid` (Critical, so it
fires out-of-band notification). The healthy agents keep running.

`dotagent mcp`'s `tools/list` is the exception: it returns an error
naming the broken files instead of a partial catalog, because a model
handed a list that quietly lost entries would answer confidently and
wrongly about what it can do.

---

## 19b. Lifecycle — agents kept alive between runs

Default is one process per event: spawn, run, exit. `[lifecycle] mode =
"persistent"` keeps the process alive and delivers requests to it, which
matters for anything holding state a fresh process would have to rebuild
(a conversation, a warm cache, an open connection). Measured on a chat
bot: 4.94s per forked message vs **1.90s** on a live process.

```toml
[lifecycle]
mode = "persistent"
key = "chat_id"          # one process per conversation; absent = one total
idle_timeout_seconds = 1800
max_invocations = 120    # recycle before a long conversation degrades it
max_instances = 8        # past this, the least recently used is evicted
startup_timeout_seconds = 30
```

The agent's shape changes with it — **one JSON object per line, both
ways**. stdout is the channel, stderr is the log:

```
→ stdin   {"v":1,"kind":"hello","agent":"x","key":"12345"}
← stdout  {"v":1,"kind":"ready","ok":true}
→ stdin   {"v":1,"kind":"request","id":"1","deadline_seconds":600,
           "trigger":{"source":"telegram","payload":{"text":"…","chat_id":12345}}}
← stdout  {"v":1,"kind":"response","id":"1","ok":true,"output":"the answer"}
```

Rules that bite if you skip them:

- **`AGENT_TRIGGER_*` does not exist here.** An environment is fixed at
  spawn and this process sees many messages; the context is in the
  `trigger` field of each request. `AGENT_LIFECYCLE=persistent` and
  `AGENT_PERSIST_KEY=<key>` are set instead.
- **`[agent] timeout_seconds` is the deadline for one request**, not the
  process lifetime. Exceeding it recycles the instance.
- **Echo `id` back.** A frame whose `id` is not the one in flight is
  dropped — that is what stops a late answer from being handed to the
  next question.
- A line that does not parse is dropped, not fatal. Put logs on stderr
  anyway.
- `AGENT_TMPDIR` belongs to the instance, so it survives between requests.
- A persistent dispatcher **without `key`** puts every conversation into
  one process, and whatever it remembers from one sender answers the
  next. `doctor` warns about it.

Minimum viable agent: `while read -r line`, answer `ready` to `hello`,
answer `{"id":…,"output":…}` to `request`. See
`examples/hello-persistent/`.

---

## 21. Sanity check before reporting "done"

When you, the LLM, generate an `agent.toml`, verify against this digest:

1. [ ] `[agent].name` is unique and matches the directory name (advisory)
2. [ ] `[run].command` resolves on `$PATH` (or is absolute)
3. [ ] At least one `[[schedules]]` with a unique `id`, unless the agent is trigger-only
4. [ ] Schedule fields match the `type`: cron needs `weekdays/hours/minute`,
   interval needs `interval_minutes`, expression needs `expression`
5. [ ] `weekdays` in `0..=6`, `hours` in `0..=23`, `minute` in `0..=59`
6. [ ] If `type = "expression"`, the syntax is systemd `OnCalendar`
   (NOT cron), and the agent is documented as Linux-only
7. [ ] Each `[[notifiers]].driver` is one of: `desktop`, `slack`, `ntfy`,
   `pushover`, `imessage`, `plugin`
8. [ ] Driver-specific required fields are present (e.g. `slack` needs
   `webhook_url`, `imessage` needs `to`, `pushover` needs `token`+`user`)
9. [ ] Plugin names in `[[preflight]]` / `[[on_*]]` exist in
   `docs/plugins/` (or are third-party plugins the user installed)
10. [ ] The agent script reads env vars (`AGENT_*`) — does NOT import an SDK
11. [ ] The agent script does NOT write to `AGENT_HEARTBEAT_FILE`
12. [ ] If you used a `[security]` block, the `network` entries match
   what the agent script actually contacts
